I’ll first read the workspace contract and the multi-wake visual-signals skill, then inspect the current rollout evidence and inherited guidance/logs before touching the controller. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult the omitted shelf or neighboring configurations.

The visual-first skill is active because the sampled examples include wake keyframes. It requires the keyframe sheets to be interpreted alongside observations, metrics, and diagnostics before any policy edit; I’m now inventorying those artifacts and reading the remaining contract/guidance in full.

The sampled set contains no collision, exit, or instability. I’ll therefore use the inherited `0.45` allocation rollout as the most informative hypothesis failure, alongside the best finite `0.35` rollout and the `0.40` anchor. This is the same evidence-handling boundary recorded by prior workers, and I’ll explicitly avoid treating it as a semantic failure.

The images and diagnostics agree on the useful mechanism: all successful policies actively swim left/down into the merged wakes, while `0.35` reaches sooner than `0.40` and lowers mean distance, effort, relative crossflow, and both joint excursions. The tradeoff is real—lateral force and moment RMS rise—so I’m treating `0.35` as a navigation/effort improvement, not a clean load improvement. I’ll record that diagnosis and make one isolated continuation of the tested allocation axis.

The candidate is now a single-axis `anterior_steering_fraction=0.30` continuation; propulsion, bearing gain/bound, phase lag, damping, and schema are unchanged. I also materially revised the durable allocation lesson to include the replicated `0.35` improvement and its force/moment tradeoff.
